title: DeepMind tests Gemini inside sealed evaluation system — Arabian Post
summary: DeepMind tests Gemini inside sealed evaluation system — Arabian Post 0 likes DeepMind tests Gemini inside sealed evaluation system 🕚 Sat 29 Aug 2026 · AP News Google DeepMind has completed what it describes as the world’s first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier-class artificia
content: DeepMind tests Gemini inside sealed evaluation system — Arabian Post ... DeepMind tests Gemini inside sealed evaluation system ... Google DeepMind has completed what it describes as the world’s first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier-class artificial intelligence model, testing Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite while preventing both the developer and external evaluators from accessing each other’s confidential material. ... DeepMind worked with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, independent evaluation organisation AVERI, privacy technology group OpenMined and benchmarking consortium MLCommons. The experiment placed Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite and confidential evaluation material inside a protected computing environment, allowing the model to process the questions without exposing them to Google and without revealing the model weights to the evaluators. ... Two evaluation exercises were conducted using Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. AVERI used previously unreleased prompts drawn from the MLCommons AILuminate safety benchmark family, while the Singapore AI Safety Institute supplied a separate confidential prompt collection. MLCommons had deliberately reserved part of its benchmark so that the material had not previously been exposed to the model being tested. ... The double-blind architecture attempts to protect both interests simultaneously. Evaluators can examine a proprietary system without receiving its underlying weights, while developers can submit a model for independent assessment without acquiring the confidential questions against which it is being measured. The arrangement could become particularly important for cybersecurity, biological-risk and government evaluations involving data too sensitive to exchange through conventional testing procedures. ... The experiment builds on earlier work involving confidential computing and AI testing. OpenMined said a 2024 project involving Anthropic and the UK AI Safety Institute explored double-blind evaluation techniques using public assets, including GPT-2 and part of a biological dataset. The new exercise differs by placing genuinely proprietary model material and unreleased evaluation data inside the protected system.

title: Google DeepMind Ran History's First AI Benchmark Evaluation Where Neither Side Could Cheat
summary: Google DeepMind Ran History's First AI Benchmark Evaluation Where Neither Side Could Cheat Deepmind.google For years, the AI evaluation industry had one structural problem no contractual safeguard could solve: whoever runs the test either has to hand the model provider the questions, or hand the e
content: For years, the AI evaluation industry had one structural problem no contractual safeguard could solve: whoever runs the test either has to hand the model provider the questions, or hand the evaluator the model. On August 27, 2026, Google DeepMind announced the world's first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier-class AI model — one that required neither compromise, using cryptographic hardware to seal Gemini's weights and an external evaluator's benchmark prompts simultaneously inside a single hardware-encrypted enclave where neither party could see the other's protected data. ... The pilot, conducted in partnership with Singapore's AI Safety Institute (AISI), privacy-computing nonprofit OpenMined, AI benchmarking consortium MLCommons, and evaluation firm AVERI, tested Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against confidential benchmarks — and its significance has nothing to do with how Gemini scored. What matters is how the test was run: for the first time in the industry's history, a model provider and an independent evaluator conducted a formal evaluation without either side needing to trust the other's word about what data they had seen. ... The solution Google DeepMind piloted relies on Google Cloud's ... Space product, running on an NVIDIA H100 80-gigabyte Confidential GPU with Intel TDX (Trust Domain Extensions) host memory encryption. ... The architecture proceeds in stages. Google DeepMind loads Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite's weights and inference code into the enclave; the evaluating organizations load their benchmark prompts and evaluation code. Both datasets travel into the enclave over encrypted connections. Once inside, the model weights sit in hardware-encrypted GPU memory and the evaluation prompts sit in encrypted host memory. At no point during the evaluation can the model provider read the prompts or the evaluator read the weights. ... transmits any sensitive data, both parties run remote attestation — a cryptographic verification step that confirms the enclave is running precisely the software both sides agreed to, not a modified version that could exfiltrate data. When the ... finishes, the evaluator ... The current pilot is therefore most directly applicable to models in the class of Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite: capable, production-class models that fit within a single GPU's memory budget. Larger models — including the flagship frontier systems that receive the most regulatory and competitive scrutiny — will require the multi-chip architecture to be engineered and validated before this approach can be extended to them.
